The third is outside Python altogether: where the platform's `time` module has the function `"tzset"`, loading a settings module put `TIME_ZONE` into the process's environment and had the C library read it (`django/conf/__init__.py:Settings.__init__`).
On the way in it does three things, in `override_settings.enable` (`django/test/utils.py:override_settings.enable`).

On the way out, `override_settings.disable` puts the earlier wrapped object back and sends the signal again for each name, with the restored value and `enter=False` (`django/test/utils.py:override_settings.disable`).

If a receiver raises, `enable` keeps the exception as `override_settings.enable_exception` and calls `disable` there and then, which raises it, so the code the override was to wrap never runs (`django/test/utils.py:override_settings.enable`).

A holder passes a read of a setting not set on it to its `default_settings` ([The settings object](settings.md#settingsconfigure-settings-without-a-module)), and an override's holder has for its `default_settings` whatever the proxy wrapped when it was made: the holder of the override it is nested in or, at the bottom, what the settings were loaded into, for a project with a settings module the `Settings`, that module over the defaults (`django/conf/__init__.py:UserSettingsHolder.__getattr__`).

`del settings.TIME_ZONE` inside both overrides marks the name deleted on the inner holder alone, and a read of it then stops there with `AttributeError`, though the `Settings` below still has it (`django/conf/__init__.py:UserSettingsHolder.__delattr__`).

The receivers in `django/test/signals.py` are connected when that module is imported, and it is imported with `django.test`.

A serving process has no reason to import `django.test`, and nothing in it would send the signal if it did: every send of `setting_changed` in Django's source is in `django/test/`, and `LazySettings.__setattr__` sends nothing.

`MIDDLEWARE` has no receiver: a handler builds its chain once, and the test client's handler builds its own at its first request, from the `MIDDLEWARE` in force then (`django/test/client.py:ClientHandler.__call__`).
`DATABASES` has one that only warns, because the connections are not rebuilt (`django/utils/connection.py:BaseConnectionHandler.settings`).

`INSTALLED_APPS` is the one setting whose override changes the app registry, and `override_settings.enable` handles it first, before it touches the settings, so that a list that cannot be loaded leaves the settings as they were (`django/test/utils.py:override_settings.enable`).

It pushes the current dictionary of application configurations onto a stack, `Apps.stored_app_configs`, empties the registry's view of what is installed, sets its three flags and `Apps.loading` back to false, and calls `Apps.populate` with the new list, so that all three phases run again ([Populating the app registry](populate.md)) (`django/apps/registry.py:Apps.set_installed_apps`); on leaving, `Apps.unset_installed_apps` pops the stack, sets the flags true again, and runs no phase (`django/apps/registry.py:Apps.unset_installed_apps`).

It pushes the current dictionary of application configurations onto a stack, `Apps.stored_app_configs`, empties the registry's view of what is installed, sets its three flags and `Apps.loading` back to false, and calls `Apps.populate` with the new list, so that all three phases run again ([Populating the app registry](populate.md)) (`django/apps/registry.py:Apps.set_installed_apps`); on leaving, `Apps.unset_installed_apps` pops the stack, sets the flags true again, and runs no phase (`django/apps/registry.py:Apps.unset_installed_apps`).

`Apps.set_available_apps`, which a `TransactionTestCase` with `available_apps` uses, only narrows the installed applications to a subset, importing nothing and calling no `ready` ([Emptying the tables after each test: `TransactionTestCase`](../testing/transaction-test-case.md#fewer-applications-available_apps)) (`django/apps/registry.py:Apps.set_available_apps`).

An override can still add models, when it installs an application whose models module was never imported, and they stay in `all_models` after `Apps.unset_installed_apps` ([The registry and its models](registry.md#two-maps-appsapp_configs-and-appsall_models)) (`django/apps/registry.py:Apps.set_installed_apps`).

`Signal.connect` adds a receiver only if its key is not already there, and a bound method's key is made from its object as well as its function, so the method of the new configuration is a receiver of its own; a function defined at a module's top level, or a dispatch uid, gives the same key each time (`django/dispatch/dispatcher.py:_make_id`, `django/dispatch/dispatcher.py:Signal.connect`).
